1.title: Too Big to Depeg
1.text: The 800-pound gorilla of stablecoins commands more market cap than most countries' GDP and settles more volume daily than Visa. Despite years of "where are the reserves?" discourse, Tether keeps printing — and keeps getting redeemed at par. Its BDO Italia attestations have quieted skeptics somewhat, but the real moat is simpler: when every exchange, DeFi protocol, and OTC desk denominates in USDT, switching costs approach infinity. Love it or hate it, the market has voted with its liquidity.

2.title: The Regulated Runner-Up
2.text: Circle's USDC is what happens when you build a stablecoin for compliance officers. Full monthly attestations from Deloitte, SEC registration, and a BlackRock-managed reserve fund make it the institutional darling of the space. The March 2023 SVB depeg briefly shattered its reputation for safety — and its market cap still hasn't fully recovered to pre-crisis levels. For anyone who needs a stablecoin their legal team won't flinch at, USDC remains the default.

146.title: The Basis Trade, Tokenized
146.text: Ethena's USDe pioneered the delta-neutral stablecoin: hold spot crypto, short the perps, pocket the funding rate. It works beautifully in bull markets when longs pay shorts handsomely for leverage. The catch? When funding flips negative — as it inevitably does — the insurance fund becomes the only thing between USDe and a death spiral. It's a sophisticated yield product wearing a stablecoin's clothing.

209.title: The Artist Formerly Known as DAI
209.text: Sky Dollar is MakerDAO's rebranded stablecoin, the culmination of Rune Christensen's "Endgame" vision to make the protocol more normie-friendly. Under the hood it's the same overcollateralized vaults and PSM modules — just with a fresh coat of paint and a governance structure that's still figuring itself out. Whether the rebrand was genius marketing or unnecessary complexity remains the market's most polite disagreement.

262.title: The Presidential Stablecoin
262.text: World Liberty Financial's USD1 is backed by the Trump family brand and entered the market with all the subtlety you'd expect. It launched with RWA backing and centralized governance, positioning itself somewhere between a political statement and a financial product. The reserves are real, but the regulatory questions write themselves.

5.title: The OG Decentralized Dollar
5.text: The stablecoin that proved crypto could create a synthetic dollar without a bank account. DAI survived the March 2020 crash, navigated the USDC depeg contagion, and maintained its peg through sheer overcollateralization. Now overshadowed by its own rebrand (USDS) and increasingly backed by RWAs rather than pure crypto collateral, DAI remains the philosophical North Star that most "decentralized" stablecoins claim to be inspired by.

120.title: Big Fintech's Entry Ticket
120.text: PayPal's stablecoin proves that when a payments giant with 400 million users issues a dollar token, people notice. Paxos-issued and fully reserved in treasuries and cash, PYUSD's regulatory credentials are impeccable. Its challenge isn't trust — it's utility. Until DeFi and PayPal's walled garden meaningfully converge, it risks being the best-credentialed stablecoin nobody uses on-chain.

246.title: The Falcon Play
246.text: Falcon Finance's USDf enters the delta-neutral arena alongside Ethena, offering yield through basis-trade strategies with a centralized-dependent governance model. Its crypto-backed structure means the peg relies on market dynamics rather than reserve transparency. In the crowded yield-bearing stablecoin space, differentiation is a question of execution speed and risk management.

237.title: Treasury Yields On-Chain
237.text: Hashnote's USYC is a tokenized money market fund that passes T-bill yields directly to holders. It's RWA-backed, yield-bearing, and about as exciting as its underlying asset — which is precisely the point. In a world of exotic DeFi yields, sometimes the most radical product is just a savings account with an ERC-20 wrapper.

286.title: The Paxos Sequel
286.text: Global Dollar is Paxos's second act after BUSD, built to avoid the regulatory friction that killed its Binance partnership. Singapore-regulated and reserve-backed, USDG targets the institutional corridor that doesn't want Tether's opacity or Circle's SVB memories. Whether the market needs another compliant stablecoin is a question USDG is determined to answer anyway.

250.title: Ripple's Dollar Bet
250.text: After years of fighting the SEC over XRP, Ripple launched its own stablecoin with NYDFS approval — a plot twist even Ripple skeptics didn't see coming. RLUSD is built for Ripple's payments network, aiming to be the bridge asset that XRP never became for institutional transfers. Fully reserved and centrally managed, it's less a DeFi primitive and more a cross-border payments tool.

129.title: Ondo's Yield Machine
129.text: Ondo Finance's USDY offers tokenized US Treasury exposure to everyone outside the US, neatly sidestepping domestic securities law. It's RWA-backed, yield-bearing, and has become the poster child of the "tokenized treasuries" narrative. The irony of a product that democratizes US government debt by excluding US persons is apparently lost on no one.

173.title: When BlackRock Calls It a Token
173.text: BlackRock's tokenized money market fund is what happens when the world's largest asset manager decides blockchain isn't a meme. BUIDL doesn't try to be a DeFi building block — it's institutional plumbing with an ERC-20 wrapper. When Larry Fink's firm validates tokenization, the rest of TradFi starts returning phone calls.

14.title: Justin Sun's Undying Dollar
14.text: USDD 2.0 emerged from its rocky algorithmic era with crypto collateral and a fresh governance model, though the centralized-dependent tag tells you Justin Sun still has the keys. It persistently trades above peg, which sounds good until you realize the premium reflects illiquidity as much as demand. The TRON ecosystem keeps it alive; whether that's a feature or a risk depends on your priors about its founder.

221.title: Ethena's Safe Side
221.text: If USDe is the exciting sibling, USDtb is the responsible one — backed by BlackRock's BUIDL fund rather than delta-neutral trades. Ethena built it for users who want the ecosystem without the basis-trade risk, creating a safety valve that also serves as USDe's backstop. It's the stablecoin equivalent of keeping a boring index fund alongside your options portfolio.

213.title: The Middleman's Stablecoin
213.text: M0's M token is a middleware play: rather than competing with USDC or USDT directly, it provides infrastructure for other stablecoins and fintechs to build on. Its RWA-backed reserves and centralized-dependent governance aim for a middle ground between Tether's opacity and Circle's centralization. The "protocol for stablecoins" pitch is elegant in theory — the question is whether the market wants a meta-stablecoin layer.

336.title: The Aggregator Dollar
336.text: United Stables takes the yield-aggregation approach, pooling reserves across multiple strategies and passing the returns to holders. It's a bet that diversification of stablecoin backing is itself a feature worth tokenizing. Simple concept, hard execution.

309.title: AI Meets RWA
309.text: USD.AI blends the two hottest crypto narratives — artificial intelligence and real-world assets — into a single stablecoin product. Its centralized-dependent governance suggests human oversight where it counts, while the AI branding does the marketing work. Whether the "AI" label reflects genuine innovation or narrative arbitrage is left as an exercise for the reader.

195.title: The Usual Suspect
195.text: Usual's USD0 burst onto the scene promising a stablecoin where revenue flows back to tokenholders via the USUAL governance token. The RWA-backed reserves provide the peg stability, while the protocol's token economics provide the sizzle. It's an interesting governance experiment, though the December 2024 USD0++ depeg reminded everyone that innovative doesn't mean risk-free.

118.title: Aave's Dollar
118.text: GHO is what happens when the largest lending protocol decides to mint its own stablecoin. Borrowers on Aave can mint GHO at favorable rates, creating a dollar tightly coupled to Aave's ecosystem health. The peg has been stable since the rocky first months, and stkAAVE discounts give governance participants a reason to borrow. It's DeFi-native in a way that few stablecoins genuinely are.

7.title: The Fallen Faithful
7.text: Once positioned as the transparent alternative to Tether, TrueUSD has fallen from grace with a market cap that's a fraction of its peak. Regulatory issues, questions about its Prime Trust relationship, and a depeg incident in 2023 eroded the trust its name once implied. It persists more as a cautionary tale about counterparty risk than as a competitive stablecoin.

119.title: Binance's Current Favorite
119.text: First Digital USD rose to prominence as Binance's preferred stablecoin after BUSD's regulatory demise. Hong Kong-based and reserve-backed, it serves as the default trading pair on the world's largest exchange. Its fate is tied to Binance's continued endorsement — a single point of dependency that the market has apparently accepted.

296.title: Cap's Yield Play
296.text: Cap Protocol's cUSD offers an RWA-backed stablecoin with a centralized-dependent governance model that routes yield back to holders. It operates in the increasingly crowded space of yield-bearing stablecoins, competing on distribution and integration rather than novelty. The protocol's bet is that a well-executed yield product can carve out space between the giants.

50.title: The Euro's Best On-Chain Bet
50.text: Circle's euro stablecoin brings the same reserve transparency and regulatory posture as USDC to the eurozone. MiCA-compliant and fully backed, EURC is positioning itself as the default EUR stablecoin before regulations force weaker competitors out. The euro stablecoin market is nascent enough that first-mover advantage still matters — and Circle is determined to be the name that sticks.

197.title: Resolving the Yield Question
197.text: Resolv's USR takes the delta-neutral approach with crypto backing, offering an alternative to Ethena's USDe for users who want basis-trade yields with a different risk profile. Its insurance pool and risk management framework attempt to address the perennial "what happens when funding goes negative" problem. In the basis-trade stablecoin niche, USR competes on risk structure rather than brand recognition.

272.title: The SEC-Registered Yield Coin
272.text: YLDS stands alone as one of the few yield-bearing stablecoins registered with the SEC as a security. This means actual regulatory clarity rather than the "move fast and hope for the best" approach most competitors take. The trade-off is operational constraints and restricted availability, but for institutions requiring regulatory certainty, YLDS is the rare stablecoin that comes with a blessing from Washington.

258.title: The Ruble's Digital Shadow
258.text: A7A5 is a ruble-pegged stablecoin that appeared seemingly from nowhere to claim a massive market cap. Its centralized governance and RWA backing make it structurally conventional, but the geopolitical context makes it anything but. In a sanctions-heavy environment, a large ruble stablecoin raises more questions than its sparse documentation answers.

249.title: Latin America's Bridge
249.text: Brazilian Digital's BRZ gives Brazil's crypto traders a real-denominated on-ramp without the volatility of converting through USD pairs. RWA-backed and centrally managed, it serves a practical need in one of crypto's most active retail markets. Its success is less about innovation and more about understanding that sometimes the simplest product wins.

66.title: Frax's Inflation Hedge
66.text: Frax Price Index is pegged not to a currency but to the CPI — a stablecoin that tries to preserve purchasing power rather than nominal value. It's algorithmic, experimental, and philosophically interesting: why peg to a dollar that loses value annually when you can peg to the cost of living? The execution challenges of maintaining a CPI peg are considerable, but the concept alone makes FPI the most intellectually honest "stable" coin in the market.

254.title: SocGen's Blockchain Experiment
254.text: EUR CoinVertible is issued by SG-FORGE, the digital asset arm of French banking giant Société Générale. It's a fully regulated, MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin from a systemically important bank — which is either the future of tokenized money or a corporate innovation lab's pet project. Either way, when a bank with over a trillion euros in assets issues a stablecoin, the industry takes notes.

147.title: The Swiss Euro
147.text: Anchored Coins' AEUR offers a Swiss-regulated, reserve-backed euro stablecoin that targets the intersection of European money and Swiss financial infrastructure. Its smaller market cap belies a clean regulatory setup. In the euro stablecoin race, AEUR competes on jurisdiction prestige rather than distribution scale.

325.title: Binance's Euro
325.text: Eurite is the euro stablecoin endorsed by Binance, giving it instant distribution to the world's largest exchange. Issued by Banking Circle and regulated in the EU, it's MiCA-ready from day one. Whether Binance's distribution muscle can make a euro stablecoin stick where others have struggled remains the open question.

226.title: Swiss Stubbornness, Tokenized
226.text: Frankencoin is a genuinely decentralized Swiss franc stablecoin — no foundation, no team tokens, no VC backing. Its auction-based liquidation mechanism and minimalist governance are a throwback to crypto's original ethos. The Swiss franc peg serves a niche audience, but Frankencoin proves that small, well-designed protocols can survive without a marketing budget.

101.title: Monerium's Electronic Money
101.text: Monerium's EURe is one of the few stablecoins licensed as electronic money in the EEA, meaning it's legally equivalent to a bank balance. It connects directly to IBAN accounts, making fiat on/off-ramps seamless in a way most stablecoins only promise. Its small scale belies its regulatory significance: EURe is what euro stablecoins look like when they actually comply with European financial law.

55.title: Angle's DeFi Euro
55.text: Angle Protocol's EURA is one of the few crypto-backed euro stablecoins — an overcollateralized design in a market dominated by RWA-backed issuers. Its centralized-dependent governance means community involvement with practical guardrails. For DeFi purists who want a euro without bank dependencies, EURA is one of the few options on the menu.
